It's not exactly like I'm staring across the table at ''Boba Fett'' or ''Bossk.'' Just a gambling addict living off cheap bounties.''"
"''Laugh it up, Khamdek. I've been disrespected my whole life—but being ''underestimated'' has its values.|Lord Khamdek and Dengar|[[Bounty Hunters 23|''Bounty Hunters'' 23]]}} '''Dengar''', also known as '''Dengar the Demolisher''', was a [[Corellia]]n [[human]] [[bounty hunter]] operating since the early stages of the [[Clone Wars]]. Dengar participated in an [[Safe cargo objective|operation]] on [[Quarzite]]—during which he served as a member of [[Krayt's Claw]], a syndicate of hunters including [[Boba Fett]], [[Bossk'wassak'Cradossk|Bossk]], and [[Asajj Ventress]]—to secure property valuable to Lord [[Otua Blank]] of the planet Quarzite. Dengar also took jobs for clients such as the [[Grand Hutt Council]], fighting against [[Maul]] and his [[Shadow Collective]] on [[Nal Hutta]]. Dengar remained active through the [[Galactic Civil War]], during which he was one of several bounty hunters hired by [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]] to capture [[Han Solo]], captain of the ''[[Millennium Falcon]]''. Though Dengar ultimately lost Vader's bounty to his rival and partner Boba Fett, he was later present with Bossk and Fett in [[Boba Fett's Palace|Jabba's Palace]] on Tatooine during Solo's rescue by [[Jedi Knight]] [[Luke Skywalker]]. Dengar's impressive longevity led him to continue his work as a bounty hunter even after the [[Galactic Empire|Empire]] was defeated at the [[Battle of Endor]]. Around a year later, he teamed up with other tenured hunters such as [[Embo]] when he joined [[Jas Emari]] and her [[Jas Emari's crew|crew]] after the [[Battle of Jakku]]. ==Biography== ===Early life=== Dengar was a [[human]] [[Gender|male]] from the [[planet]] [[Corellia]]. However, little was known of his early life.[[:File:StarWars2020-18-Handbook.png]] As a [[Youngling|child]], he raced [[swoop]] [[speeder bike]]s in Corellia's [[swoop racing]] scene. He had a friend named [[Hill Purpura]], with whom he competed in swoop racing. Both would later make differing claims as to which of them won more often.[[Bounty Hunters 10|''Bounty Hunters'' 10]] Dengar would later claim he had been a professional [[swoop]] bike [[racer]]. Before Dengar became a [[bounty hunter]], he served as a [[gladiator]].''[[Star Wars: Scum and Villainy: Case Files on the Galaxy's Most Notorious]]'' It was during the earliest [[Standard day|days]] of that war that he began [[Hunter|hunting]] [[Bounty|bounties]]. ===The Clone Wars=== ====Safe cargo objective==== {{Quote|So... what do you think is in that box?''"
"''Whatever it is, it better be worth all this effort.|Dengar and Asajj Ventress contemplate the contents of the box|}} As part of [[Krayt's Claw]], Dengar was part of an [[Safe cargo objective|operation]] alongside fellow hunters [[Boba Fett]], [[Bossk'wassak'Cradossk|Bossk]], [[Latts Razzi]], [[C-21 Highsinger]], and [[Oked]]. The hunters were hired to escort a [[subtram]] containing [[Pluma Sodi|cargo]] valuable to [[Otua Blank]], the leader of the [[Belugan]] people of [[Quarzite]]. While preparing for the mission in [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina]], Oked was [[Death|murdered]] by the wayward [[Dark side of the Force|dark side]] user [[Asajj Ventress]], who promptly agreed to take the dead hunter's place on the mission roster. [[File:DengarKageFight-Bounty.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Dengar fights a Kage Warrior]] Dengar and company set off in Bossk's [[Starship|ship]], the ''[[Hound's Tooth]]'', to Quarzite, where the Belugan [[Major]] [[Rigosso]] transported the team to the train's subterranean loading dock via a space [[Turbolift|elevator]] from an orbital skyhook. Dengar, along with Ventress, were assigned to guard the rear of the train. After unsuccessfully flirting with Ventress, a team of skilled [[Kage Warriors]] boarded the train in an attempt to retrieve the cargo. Dengar managed to fight off many of the attackers due to his skilled [[Unarmed combat|hand-to-hand combat]] techniques, and even managed to kill two using [[sticky explosive]]s. Dengar was eventually overwhelmed by the attackers and was thrown from the train, landing safely on the subterranean surface. Dengar and his allies, who were likewise thrown from the train, returned to the skyhook to await Ventress, who had betrayed the mission objective by swapping the cargo with Boba Fett, who was bound and gagged. Before departing, she hands over the rest of the team's share of unmarked [[Galactic Credit Standard|credits]]. ====Working for the Hutts==== {{Quote|Come on, let's get out of here.|Latts Razzi, to her team after their job for the Hutts went south|}} [[File:Crime_Lord_SWDConv.png|thumb|right|250px|Dengar was on the payroll of the Hutts]] Dengar was later employed by the [[Hutt]]s alongside Latts, [[Embo]], and [[Sugi (bounty hunter)|Sugi]] as protection on [[Nal Hutta]]. They were present when the renegade [[Sith Lord]]s [[Maul]] and [[Savage Opress]] as well as the [[Death Watch]] leader [[Pre Vizsla]] [[Mission to Nal Hutta|came]] to ally with the Hutts. When the plan went sour, the four bounty hunters attacked, though they were pushed by the [[Mandalorian]]'s [[flamethrower]]. The trio soon received reinforcements and attacked. When the battle was clearly lost, Dengar and Latts saved the beaten Embo and Sugi by covering their escape with [[Smoke grenade|smoke bombs]]. The group of mercenaries fled the Death Watch and their [[Sith]] allies. ====War's end==== Around the time of the end of the Clone Wars, Dengar disappeared from circulation for a brief period of time, and was believed to have been recovering from a near-fatal injury. ===Galactic Civil War=== ====The Hidden Hand==== {{Quote|The Hidden Hand.''"
"''Told you everything I know about those maniacs. And I ''guarantee'' what I said is more than you'll ''ever'' get out of ''him''. Valence won't talk. He's too dumb.''"
"''You are free to go, bounty hunter. Should the Empire require your services again…I know where to find you.|Darth Vader and Dengar|[[Target Vader 5|''Target Vader'' 5]]}} In [[1 BBY]],''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of ''Target Vader'' to [[1 BBY]]. Dengar joined a [[Beilert Valance's crew|team]] of bounty hunters under [[Beilert Valance]] who were hired by the [[Hidden Hand]] to assassinate Darth Vader, as a secret informant for Vader himself. Dengar and the others went with Valance aboard the ''[[Broken Wing]]'' and got weapons from [[Fetya]] on [[Arvina]] However, Fetya double crossed them, but were saved when Vader's star destroyer opened fired on them. Dengar and the group survived and stole a [[K79-S80 Imperial Troop Transport|ITT]]. They used it to return to the ''Broken Wing''.[[Target Vader 2|''Target Vader'' 2]] Dengar and the others went to [[Heva]] and asked about the Hidden Hand. However, Vader and his destroyer arrived. Dengar went with [[Honnah]] to prepare a trap for Vader. He watched as the Broken Wing took on Vader's [[Darth Vader's TIE Advanced|TIE Advanced]] and several other TIEs. After Valance crashed his ship, Dengar and Honnah took aim at Vader[[Target Vader 3|''Target Vader'' 3]] and waited for Valance to give the signal to eliminate him. Dengar opened fire on Vader while Honnah took Vader head on with her battle-ax. After Honnah and the others were killed by Vader, Dengar revealed he was working for Vader by stunning Valance as stormtroopers arrived.[[Target Vader 4|''Target Vader'' 4]] Aboard Vader's destroyer, Dengar told Vader everything he knew and learned about the Hidden Hand before he left for Coruscant. He was then confronted by Valance. Dengar was punched hard by Valance, but was allowed to live despite his betrayal of Valance and his crew.[[Target Vader 6|''Target Vader'' 6]] ====The Smuggler's Moon==== {{Quote|You know what? Maybe I ''don't'' want you so alive after all. Just tell me one thing, and I'll put you out of your filthy, stinking misery. ''Where is Han Solo?!"
"''Right ''here'', ugly.|Dengar, interrogating a fallen Chewbacca, is ambushed by Han Solo|[[Star Wars (2015) 11|''Star Wars'' (2015) 11]]}} Though weathered and grizzled by [[Standard year|years]] of bounty hunting, Dengar was still active around the time of the [[Assault on Cymoon|assault]] on [[Cymoon 1]]. He was present in [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure|Jabba's]] court when [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]], on a mission to negotiate with the Hutt, arrived at the [[crime lord]]'s [[Boba Fett's Palace|palace]]. Jabba was briefly [[Force choke]]d by the [[Sith Lord]] and after this Jabba ordered Dengar out the of room so that "negotiations" could commence.[[Darth Vader (2015) 1|''Darth Vader'' (2015) 1]] Following this, Dengar visited a cantina on [[Nar Shaddaa]], the notorious [[moon]] of the planet [[Nal Hutta]], where he was informed by a [[Gungan]] that [[Chewbacca]] was present. Dengar soon located the Wookiee, before shocking him as he and [[C-3PO]] were about to storm [[Grakkus Jahibakti Tingi|Grakkus]] the Hutt's [[Palace of Grakkus the Hutt|palace]]. He greeted Chewbacca, claiming that Jabba sent his regards, before turning to 3PO and demanding to know where Han Solo was. 3PO told the bounty hunter that Solo was not with them, prompting Dengar to order him to contact the smuggler. 3PO agreed to comply, but first attempted to save Chewbacca. Before Dengar could intervene, the protocol droid had shorted out the shock bolt, and Chewbacca rose up to his feet. The two then began to fight on the rooftops. Dengar told Chewbacca that he could throw a punch just as well as the Wookiee, before being knocked backwards by a successful hit. Dengar then grabbed a blaster, before Chewbacca crushed it, and grabbed the corellian by the neck, raising him off the ground. [[File:SoloShotsDengar-2015StarWars11.jpg|thumb|left|250x250px|Dengar is shot in the back by Han Solo]] Dengar ignited an explosive, knocking Chewbacca to the floor, before threatening to use his vibroblade against him. Dengar again knocked Chewbacca back, taunting him claiming he defied the reputation Wookiees had for being mighty warriors, before being punched up the chin. Fed up, Dengar threatened to kill the Wookiee, but first demanded the location of Solo. In that moment, Solo shot Dengar in the back revealing himself to be behind the bounty hunter, before ordering that he take his hands off of Chewbacca. Solo stated that Dengar was outgunned, and once again ordered him to step away from the Wookiee. Solo friend Princess Leia Organa of [[Alderaan]] advised Dengar to listen to Solo, stating that his wife would be eager to shoot him. Though Dengar was confused, his rage took priority, and he held up a thermal detonator, stating that they would all die if he were to let go, and stated that he and Solo step aside to settle it like men. Before he could finish his sentence however, Chewbacca raised the bounty hunter off of the ground and launched him off the building with his thermal detonator, which proceeded to explode.[[Star Wars (2015) 12|''Star Wars'' (2015) 12]] Despite this however, Dengar managed to survive the encounter. ====In Vader's employ==== {{Quote|There will be a substantial reward for the one who finds the ''Millennium Falcon''. You are free to use any methods necessary, but I want them alive.|Darth Vader to Dengar and five other bounty hunters|{{Film|V}}}} Having survived his encounter with Chewbacca, Dengar was later secretly hired by [[Darth]] Vader along with [[Krrsantan]], [[Zuckuss]], [[Beebox]], [[IG-90]], and C-21 Highsinger to find and return [[Doctor|Dr.]] [[Chelli Lona Aphra|Aphra]].[[Darth Vader (2015) 16|''Darth Vader'' (2015) 16]] Dengar attempted to collect a bounty on [[Jaxxon T. Tumperakki]] on [[Rekelos]] by using a [[Concussion grenade]]. He later caught up with Jaxxon and his ex-girlfriend [[Amaiza Foxtrain]] on [[Valtos]]. Dengar was knocked out by Amaiza. Despite that, he was able to pick himself and decided to collect on Foxtrain's [[Holopuck|bounty puck]].{{IDWAdventuresCite-2020|annual=2020|story=Rabbit Hunt}} At some point, Dengar began dating an [[Aruzan]] woman named [[Manaroo]],''[[Starships and Speeders]]'' who became indebted to Jabba.[[Bounty Hunters 16|''Bounty Hunters'' 16]] As such, she was imprisoned in Jabba's palace, leaving her to be used as leverage against Dengar.[[Bounty Hunters 14|''Bounty Hunters'' 14]] [[File:BountyHunters.jpg|thumb|right|220px|Dengar on the bridge of the ''Executor'' in 3 ABY]] In [[3 ABY]], Dengar was one of the bounty hunters, alongside Boba Fett, Bossk, [[IG-88B|IG-88]], [[4-LOM]], and Zuckuss, summoned to the ''[[Executor]]'', the [[Galactic Empire|Imperial]] [[flagship]] of Darth Vader, who resorted to using hunters to track down the ''Millennium Falcon'', the ship of [[Captain]] Han Solo, who slipped away from Vader during the evacuation of [[Hoth]]. Dengar lost out on the Solo bounty to Fett, who delivered the now [[carbonite]]-encased Solo to the Hutt crime lord Jabba on [[Tatooine]]. ====Reunion with Valance and the quest for Solo==== Dengar was later captured by the reformed [[Ohnaka Gang]], to whom he owed a debt.[[Bounty Hunters 9|''Bounty Hunters'' 9]] Soon reunited with and put at the mercy of Beilert Valance during an operation involving the rebel transport ''[[Spirit of Jedha]]'' under his old friend Hill Purpura, Dengar agreed to help Valance track down Han Solo, repayment for selling out Valance to Darth Vader the last time they met.[[Bounty Hunters 11|''Bounty Hunters'' 11]] As they approached Nar Shaddaa, Dengar and Valance came under attack by [[Zuckuss]] and [[4-LOM]]'s ship. Dengar then held Valance at gunpoint when he refused to reveal the location of [[Cadeliah]]. He then knocked Valance out when he ran into several [[Exogorth]]s. Dengar told them that the girl was not aboard the ship, but he would them information on Fett's current whereabouts.[[Bounty Hunters 12|''Bounty Hunters'' 12]] The two bounty hunters then went to the arms market on Nar Shadaa to find Fett. However, Fett was gone by the time Dengar and Valance arrived. Dengar then spoke with [[Devono Vix]]. Valance punched Vix and Dengar tried to convince him to reveal Fett's whereabouts. Vix refused and ordered both him and Valance to be killed. The two of them fought Vix's thugs and then pursued him. When Valance ran into Chewbacca, Dengar went into a tavern for a drink. He was then strangled by Chewbacca, due to their previous encounter on Nar Shadaa. He tried to shoot the Wookiee, but was tossed at C-3PO. He woke up when Chewbacca left Valance to continue his search for Solo. Due to Valance's interrogation of Vix, Dengar and Valance were able to learn that Crimson Dawn had Solo and Fett was going after them. Dengar refused to believe him about Crimson Dawn's return until Vix was killed. Dengar saved Valance from an assassin.[[Bounty Hunters 13|''Bounty Hunters'' 13]] [[File:BountyHunters15-textless.png|thumb|left|250px|Dengar and Valance in the crosshairs of Deathstick]] Dengar and Valance were able to lose the assassin. Dengar took Valance to mechanic [[Mama Stammoch]] and her crew. As Valance was being fixed up, Dengar contacted [[Bib Fortuna]] about the status of [[Manaroo]], his girlfriend. Fortuna threatened to have her fed to the Rancor if he did not collect the bounty on Fett. Dengar learned about Crimson Dawn's origins from Stammoch. After Valance recovered, Dengar showed Stammoch a hologram of the assassin, who she recognized as [[Deathstick]]. Dengar then came under attack by Deathstick who killed Stammoch and her crew. The two bounty hunters were able to make their escape in a speeder by throwing a thermal detonator at Deathstick. Unfortunately, the speeder was not fixed and Dengar was saved from the crash when Valance grabbed him and jumped to safety. However, Deathstick followed them. Dengar and Valance took a [[Star Commuter 2000]] to [[Canto Bight]] despite it being a two day journey to get the ''[[Punishing One]]'' back. On Canto Bright, Dengar was able to get his back from [[Just Lucky]] and his boss the [[Sixth Kin]]'s leader [[Wen Delphis]]. As Dengar and Valance returned to the ''Punishing One'', they came under attack once again by Deathstick. The two fought Deathstick pushed Valance into a casino. When Valance returned, Dengar revealed that he stole Deathstick's Crimson Dawn invitation during the fight.[[Bounty Hunters 15|''Bounty Hunters'' 15]] Dengar and Valance was able to catch up with Fett on [[Jekara]]. Unfortunately, Fett was able to escape them and Dengar was trapped on a iceberg drifting away. Valance chose to leave Dengar drifting away and joined Fett in claiming Solo.[[War of the Bounty Hunters 4|''War of the Bounty Hunters'' 4]] He watched as Valance left with Fett aboard ''Slave I''. He then came under attack by a [[Zugorak]]. He only had a knife to defend himself with. However, he was saved from the creature by Deathstick, who offered to pay off Manaroo's debt to Jabba. Dengar also provided her with Valance's transmission to Yuralla Vega so she could find [[Cadeliah]] at her rebel cell base. Dengar was later present at Jabba the Hutt's palace when Fett brought in Solo. Dengar and Fett exchanged insults before Dengar pointed out that Fett was being used by the Hutt, pointing to Solo and noting that Jabba would even turn on his best smuggler. Dengar and Fett then made a bet, with Dengar wagering twenty credits that the rebels would not come to rescue Solo.{{StoryCite|story=Reputation (Boba Fett)|book=From a Certain Point of View: Return of the Jedi}} ====Revnog rampage==== {{Quote|You are suggesting that your client, who according to my notes is often known by the sobriquet ''Dengar the Demolisher''…did ''not'' simply become deeply intoxicated, steal a ''speeder'' and go for a joyride that caused immense ''vehicular mayhem''…but was instead ''hypnotized'' by a ''Jedi Knight'' who ''forced'' him to do these things?''"
"''Well, your honor, the galaxy's a big place. Who's to say there ''aren't'' Jedi out there? I'm sure you've heard the same rumors I have. What happened to my client is unusual, certainly, but not ''impossible''. I mean, here's the bottom line…you can't exactly prove it ''didn't'' happen that way, right?''"
"''Actually, Advocate Georgio, I can. The official, ''legal'' position of the Empire is that the Jedi Order, and the Jedi themselves, no longer exist. Therefore, your version of events is, in fact, ''impossible''. I sentence defendant Dengar to a fine of fifty thousand credits plus sixty days hard labor in the ''orgonium mines''. My understanding is they have a near-infinite supply of large, heavy boulders that need '' demolishing'' in those mines. I'm sure he'll fit in well.''"
"''Oh, come ''on''.|A judge and Advocate Salli Georgio, and Dengar's reaction|{{StoryCite|story=A Trick of the Mind|book=Revelations (2023) 1}}}} On [[D'Assem]], Dengar visited the planet's[[Bounty Hunters 35|''Bounty Hunters'' 35]] [[Black-Market District]]. Ingesting two bottles of [[revnog]], the bounty hunter stole a speeder and destroyed half of the port district before he was stopped by the authorities. Brought before [[Unidentified judge (Dengar)|a judge]], Dengar was represented by Advocate [[Salli Georgio]], who considered him lucky that she had agreed to work on his behalf. The trial commenced at the [[Imperial Court of Criminal Justice]] on [[Samaria]]. Georgio argued to the judge that Dengar was approached by a [[Jedi]] and put under the influence of a [[mind trick]], inciting Dengar's destructive rampage as a distraction from the Jedi's own activities. The judge, noting Dengar's epithet of "the Demolisher," found it unlikely that the bounty hunter had not simply become intoxicated and acted of his own accord. When Georgio lobbied that the scenario was not impossible and ultimately could not be disproven, the judge presented the Empire's legal position that both the Jedi and the [[Jedi Order]] no longer existed and sentenced Dengar to a 50,000 credit fine and 60 days of hard labor in the [[orgonium mines]], the frustrated defendant placing his head in his hands. Imprisoned, Dengar later berated Georgio's choice of arguing with the Jedi mind trick. Georgio reminded Dengar of the severity of what had transpired, remarking that his case had required out-of-the-box thinking. Calling Georgio the worst lawyer in the galaxy and warning her to watch herself upon his release, Dengar was dragged away by the bailiff. Georgio considered sending Dengar's bill to the mine and, contacted by a [[Landonis Balthazar Calrissian|prospective client]], said that she was now free. ====Demolished==== {{Quote|Jabba said alive, but he didn't say unscathed. Gonna enjoy carving out that smug look from your face, you glob of ''Mantellian Savrip'' vomit! I owe you for leaving me behind on that ice ''floe in ''[sic]'' Jekara''.''"
"''Yeah…sorry about that, ''Dengar''.''"
"''''Sorry?'' I had to kill a giant ''apexathor'' with a knife smaller than this one! I've been trained by the ''gurus of the assassin guild'' in ''twelve forms'' of bladed combat. Your face will be hacked to pieces before you even know what hit—''"
"''And sorry about ''this''.''"
"''—youuuuuuuuu…|Dengar and Valence; the latter knocked the former out cold|[[Bounty Hunters 42|''Bounty Hunters'' 42]]}} Dengar was present at Jabba's palace when a trader from [[Mos Elrey]] under the Hutt's protection approached with a dispute, claiming that a Trandoshan clan stole from the [[Snivvian]]'s stores. Jabba sentenced the Trandoshan to his torture chambers, though prepared to have the Snivvian killed to secure an offered ten-percent bonus from the clan. Interrupted by the arrival of Beilert Valance, Jabba offered his good graces and 50,000 credits to whomever captured Valance for further torture. Ignoring Manaroo's warning, an eager Dengar confronted Valance, intending to brutalize the cyborg for abandoning him on Jekara. Valance apologized to Dengar who, claiming to have killed an apexathor and been trained in twelve forms of bladed combat, was quickly knocked unconscious in one punch, exasperating Manaroo. Dengar later stole a shipment of spice wine from an Imperial officer, attracting the Empire's attention. Dengar, Fett, and Bossk were in the palace when chaos broke loose after the [[Jedi Knight]] [[Luke Skywalker]] arrived to [[Rescue of Han Solo|free]] Solo.{{Film|VI}} When Jabba's court left to the [[Great Pit of Carkoon]], Dengar decided not to go, a decision that saved his life because{{HelmetCollectionCite|14|Databank A-Z}} the crime lord's [[sail barge]], the ''[[Khetanna]]'', was destroyed by Skywalker and his allies. ===New Republic=== ====Skirmish on Corellia==== {{Quote|Things are changing now. Our profession is about to get marginalized, too. Those rebels won't put up with our special brand of sauce for too long, will they? It's why we gotta band together. Form a proper union. We'll be a force to reckon with.|Dengar, to [[Mercurial Swift]]|[[Aftermath (novel)|''Aftermath'']]}} [[File:MercurialVsDengar-GalacticAtlasUpdated.png|thumb|right|300px|Dengar comes to blows with the younger bounty hunter Mercurial Swift.]] Some time after the [[Battle of Endor]], which saw the death of Emperor Palpatine and allowed the suddenly winning Rebel Alliance a chance to become the [[New Republic]], Dengar got into a fight with the young bounty hunter [[Mercurial Swift]], in a holoplex rooftop on [[Coronet City]], Corellia. Dengar offered guidance, trying to convince him to join a bounty hunter alliance, but Mercurial refused, claiming he was old and ineffective. Dengar managed to have the advantage, aiming his [[particle array gun]] at his opponent, but was easily distracted and taken down when the hunter pretended to see Boba Fett standing behind him. Mercurial let him live, claiming to have no reason to kill him without a [[bounty]] to his head. The two hunters went on their separate paths, but not before Dengar gave him one last warning, saying times would be different for their kind with the New Republic in power, with the new government potentially forcing bounties on other bounty hunters. Dengar's prediction began to come true when the New Republic began denying services to bounty hunters due to the paranoia following the [[terrorist]] [[Attack on Chandrila|attacks]] that took place on [[Liberation Day (New Republic)|Liberation Day]].''[[Aftermath: Life Debt]]'' ====Working for Mercurial Swift==== {{Quote|You forgot one part.''"
"''What?''"
"''We don't really like you.|Dengar turning against Mercurial Swift|}} [[File:Dengar_SaV.png|thumb|left|200px|Dengar stands over two victims]] In the days leading up to the [[Battle of Jakku]], Dengar along with his fellow bounty hunters Embo and the [[Rodian]] [[Jeeta]] accepted work as Mercurial Swift's crew. Swift wanted to collect the [[Black Sun]] crime boss [[Gyuti]]'s bounty on the [[Zabrak]] [[Jas Emari]], the niece of the hunter Sugi. In the past, Dengar had once worked with Sugi, who had always hated Dengar. Dengar in turn was unpopular among many of his fellow bounty hunters including Swift. After learning that the Hutt crime lady [[Niima]] had taken Jas captive, Dengar and his fellow bounty hunters traveled to Niima's temple of the [[Inner Rim Territories|Inner Rim]] world of [[Jakku]] to take Jas into custody. However, Jas escaped from her captors and wounded Swift. She then managed to convince Embo, who was a friend of her aunt Sugi, to allow her to escape in Swift's [[Corellian shuttle]]. Dengar rushed back to the ship to apprehend her but was unable to stop Jas from escaping. After Jas returned with her friend [[Norra Wexley]] and the [[B1-series battle droid]] [[Mister Bones]] to Niima's temple, Dengar and his fellow hunters cornered Niima and Jas. Niima had earlier agreed to provide Jas and Norra with Imperial uniforms, an Imperial shuttle, and clearance codes to enter the [[Main Imperial base]] on Jakku out of gratitude for ferrying her back to her temple. Niima initially refused to hand over Jas and grabbed Swift by the neck. However, Dengar pointed his blaster at Niima's throat and forced the Hutt to give up Jas. While the hunters were preoccupied, Norra and Bones escaped on the Imperial shuttle. ====Teaming up with Jas Emari==== {{Quote|Times, they are a-changing, my little gompers. We're gonna need to watch each others' backs, eh?|Dengar on striking a deal with Jas Emari|}} [[File:Dengar-Conv.png|thumb|right|180px|Dengar worked with Jas Emari for the New Republic]] After taking Jas captive, Dengar and his fellow hunters returned to Swift's shuttle. Swift wanted to depart for Nar Shaddaa to hand Jas to Gyuti but was forced to delay his departure due to the Battle of Jakku. While Jeeta landed the ship in a canyon, Jas tormented Swift. Dengar then demanded that Swift tell them his plan. When an enraged Swift struck Jas, Dengar mocked Swift, who had sustained a facial scar from Jas' horns. Despite Swift's objections, Dengar indicated that he was willing to listen to Jas' counter-offer. Dengar and Embo reacted positively to Jas' offer that the New Republic would reward them for helping to capture the Imperial [[Grand Admiral]] [[Rae Sloane]], the alleged mastermind behind the Liberation Day attacks. When Dengar opined that working for the New Republic was not exactly "cozy-making," Jas promised to secure them full pardons if they worked with her. Jas also promised to share the money with Dengar and Embo. Swift tried to reassert his authority but Dengar countered that he and Embo did not like him. Dengar clubbed Swift in the head with his blaster. Swift managed to grab Jas by the neck and take her hostage. However, the Zabrak headbutted Swift and then punched him in the middle before throwing him out of the shuttle's door. Disliking Swift and accepting Jas' offer, Dengar complimented her. Embo also expressed agreement. Jeeta, who was piloting the ship, also agreed to to work for Jas. Jas and [[Jas Emari's crew|her new crew]] then flew to the [[Jakku Observatory]] where they evacuated Norra. The Battle of Jakku ultimately ended the [[Galactic Civil War]] as a New Republic victory. Following the signing of the [[Galactic Concordance]], Jas managed to secure Dengar, Embo, and Jeeta full pardons and some money from the New Republic. While it was not a huge sum, the money was enough to stop them from killing her and to convince Dengar and his fellow hunters to continue working as Jas' crew. Dengar was particularly pleased by this turn of events and remarked that they needed to watch each others' backs because times were changing. ===Cybernetic surgery=== At some point after the Galactic Civil War, Dengar underwent [[Cybernetics|cybernetic]] surgery in an attempt to remain competitive. The surgery left him barely recognizable. Some rumors claimed Dengar in fact became the hunter [[Rothgar Deng]].{{EncyclopediaCite|Din Djarin and Other Characters of the Underworld}} During the [[First Order-Resistance War]], [[Rey Skywalker|Rey]] listed Deng along with other bounty hunters who had attempted to capture [[Moebin Faltus]]. But when repeating the names, the bounty hunter [[Kief Varris]] called Deng, "Dengar."{{IDWAdventuresCite-2020|issue=14|story=Repair Stop, Part II}} ==Personality and traits== {{Quote|You made the ''wrong'' call, Valance! I can't believe you betrayed me, you veermok spore! Not that I wasn't planning to betray ''you''. But ''that's not the point''.|Dengar|}} [[File:Dengar-TCW.png|thumb|left|180px|Dengar wore plated armor and carried a heavy blaster rifle.]] Though considered by others to be crude and slovenly, Dengar thought highly of himself, often flirting with females, such as Asajj Ventress. His confidence translated into his battle tactics, often taking the fight to the enemy head on with sheer firepower and destruction, which contrasted with the more cunning tactics of hunters like [[Cad Bane]] and Boba Fett. Dengar was known to be quite brutal in combat, going so far as to rush his enemies and beat them to death with his [[heavy blaster rifle]]. He was known to rush into battle with a joy that made veteran mercenaries wonder about his life expectancy. Thanks to his brutality and cunning, Dengar was able to regularly work with Hutt contracts, even often working alone on these missions. In addition, he was held in high regard by Fett for his excellent track record of hunting down his marks. Despite working for crime lords like Jabba, Dengar did not trust them, knowing one failure could lead to his end. While Dengar worked with several bounty hunters, including Sugi and Mercurial Swift, he was widely disliked by them. Dengar in turn disliked Swift, regarding the younger bounty hunter as arrogant and opportunistic. Jas Emari managed to convince Dengar and his companions Embo and Jeeta to turn against Swift with the promise of financial rewards from the New Republic for hunting down Grand Admiral Sloane and securing full pardons. Dengar knew how to fire a blaster and was also familiar with melee combat. Dengar was a human male who was 1.87 [[meter]]s (6 [[Foot|feet]], 2 inches) tall, He had [[Color|brown]] [[hair]], blue [[eye]]s and light skin. Much of Dengar's body was covered in cybernetics. ==Skills and abilities== {{Quote|I'm not just a ''pretty face,'' you know. I can throw a ''punch'' as well as you ca--|Dengar, to Chewbacca|}} Dengar was capable in melee combat, as well as armed combat and infiltration. He had an impressive track record of hunting down his bounties. ==Equipment== {{Quote|Like I said. More toys.|Dengar attacks Chewbacca with an explosive|}} [[File:DengarsFireBlade-Conv.png|thumb|right|250px|Dengar wielding his fire blade]] Dengar wore plated battle [[armor]] and a turban to cover his head during his missions, a uniform that became very battered by the time he was summoned to Darth Vader's Super Star Destroyer.{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/bounty-episode-guide|text="Bounty" Episode Guide | The Clone Wars}} In the Clone Wars, he carried a [[DLT-18 laser rifle]] during the [[safe cargo objective]]. His preferred choice of weapon during the time of the Galactic Civil War was a [[DLT-19 heavy blaster rifle]], which was supplemented by the use of mini-grenades in close quarters combat. He also holstered a [[DL-21 blaster pistol]] and equipped himself with smoke grenades, which he used to cover his team's escape after a job for the Hutts went south, as well as a [[fire blade]].{{Destiny|set=Convergence|cardname=Dengar's Fire Blade|link=https://swdestinydb.com/card/09050}} Dengar owned a modified [[JumpMaster 5000|Jumpmaster 5000]] called the ''[[Punishing One]]''.''[[Allies and Adversaries]]'' ==Behind the scenes== ===Development=== {{Quote|Who doesn't love a good punch to Dengar's face?|Ethan Sacks|{{Twitter|ethanjsacks|status/1748127792166780978|[[Ethan Sacks]]|quote=Who doesn't love a good punch to Dengar's face?|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/LNZU2}}}} Dengar was played by British actor [[Morris Bush]] in [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']]. In two episodes of the ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' TV series, Dengar was voiced by British actor [[Simon Pegg]], who went on to reprise the role in the video game ''[[Star Wars Battlefront]]''.''[[Star Wars Battlefront]]'' In the fourth draft of ''The Empire Strikes Back'' screenplay, Dengar was described, along with Zuckuss, as "battle-scarred, mangy human types."''[[Star Wars: The Annotated Screenplays]]'' Author [[Ethan Sacks]] of ''[[Star Wars: Bounty Hunters]]'' confessed that, if Dengar was not confirmed to survive after ''Return of the Jedi'' by ''[[Star Wars: The Aftermath Trilogy|The Aftermath Trilogy]]'' of novels, he would have killed the character.{{Twitter|ethanjsacks|status/1685058324776062976|[[Ethan Sacks]]|quote=If I could have done that, I would have. But we know he’s alive in Aftermath era. {{C|In response to: "dengar death !"}}|archivedate=20230731162152}} While no explicit connection was made, Rothgar Deng's name, background, and [[armor]] resemble that of Dengar.''[[Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary]]'' The [[2020]] reference text ''[[The Star Wars Book]]'' provided further similarities, stating that Dengar became almost unrecognizable after undergoing extreme surgeries following the [[Galactic Civil War]]. The [[2021]] reference book "[[Din Djarin and Other Characters of the Underworld]]" went even further, adding that an [[in-universe]] rumor stated that Deng was in fact Dengar. ===The Freemaker Adventures=== [[File:Dengar_and_company_Showdown.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Dengar, flanked by Baash and Raam, in the ''Freemaker Adventures'']] Dengar is a secondary antagonist in the non-[[canon]] [[Disney XD]] animated television series ''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Freemaker Adventures]]'', which ran between [[June 20]] and [[August 29]], [[2016]] portrayed by [[James Patrick Stuart]]. In the series, he works for the Hutt crime lord [[Graballa/LEGO|Graballa]], who is obsessed with finding the protagonist [[Rowan Freemaker/LEGO|Rowan Freemaker]]. The [[Force-sensitive]] Rowan is on a quest to find the scattered [[Kyber crystal]] that make up the [[Kyber Saber]], a powerful ancient [[Jedi]] weapon.{{FreemakerAdventures|The Lost Treasure of Cloud City}} Graballa wants to obtain these kyber crystals in order to finance a beach resort and café. In the series, Dengar is aided by the [[Iktotchi]] bounty hunters [[Baash]] and [[Raam]].{{FreemakerAdventures|Race on Tatooine}} Graballa later teams up with the Sith acolyte [[Naare]] in exchange for sharing half of the Kyber Saber crystals.{{FreemakerAdventures|The Test}} However, Naare double crosses them and drives them away.{{FreemakerAdventures|Duel of Destiny}} Graballa and his henchmen then exact their revenge by freezing Naare in carbonite.{{FreemakerAdventures|Return of the Kyber Saber}} Dengar also appeared as a downloadable character within the video game ''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Force Awakens]]''. Dengar resurfaces as a secondary antagonist in the [[LEGO Star Wars: The Freemaker Adventures Season Two|second season]] of the ''Freemaker Adventures'', which aired between [[June 17]] and [[August 16]], [[2017]]. In the series, Dengar is still serving Graballa and becomes one of the Freemakers' obstacles during their [[Mission to obtain Embersteel wings]]. Graballa is depicted as having a tense relationship with Dengar, regarding him as a "freeloader."{{FreemakerAdventures|The Embersteel Blade}} Under Graballa's orders, Dengar later leads a team of bounty hunters consisting of IG-88, Bossk, 4-LOM, and Zuckuss to apprehend the Freemakers at the Wheel. However, the Freemakers managed to elude the bounty hunters and also [[Mission to obtain an energy matrix activator|obtain]] the energy matrix activator needed to build the [[Arrowhead (Freemakers)|''Arrowhead'']].{{FreemakerAdventures|Return to the Wheel}} ==Appearances== {{ScrollBox| {{Mediacat|imagecat=Images of Dengar}} *''[[Star Wars: Force Arena]]'' *''[[Star Wars: Galactic Defense]]'' *''[[Star Wars Battlefront II]]'' {{Mo}} *{{TCW|Bounty (episode)}} *{{StoryCite|story=The Lost Nightsister|book=The Clone Wars: Stories of Light and Dark|audiobook=1}} *{{TCW|Eminence (episode)}} *{{StoryCite|story=The Long Game (comic story)|book=Age of Rebellion Special 1}} *[[Target Vader 1|''Target Vader'' 1]] *[[Target Vader 2|''Target Vader'' 2]] *[[Target Vader 3|''Target Vader'' 3]] *[[Target Vader 4|''Target Vader'' 4]] *[[Target Vader 5|''Target Vader'' 5]] *[[Target Vader 6|''Target Vader'' 6]] *{{StoryCite|story=The Sand Will Provide|book=Star Wars (2015) 37}} *''[[Star Wars: The Original Trilogy – A Graphic Novel]]'' *''[[Star Wars Battlefront]]'' {{DLC}} *[[Lando 3|''Lando'' 3]] {{C|Variant cover only}} *{{IDWAdventuresCite-2020|annual=2020|story=Rabbit Hunt}} *[[Darth Vader (2015) 1|''Darth Vader'' (2015) 1]] *[[Star Wars (2015) 10|''Star Wars'' (2015) 10]] *[[Star Wars (2015) 11|''Star Wars'' (2015) 11]] *[[Star Wars (2015) 12|''Star Wars'' (2015) 12]] *[[Darth Vader (2015) 16|''Darth Vader'' (2015) 16]] *{{IDWAdventuresCite-2020|annual=2020|story=A Rebel Bounty}} *{{Film|V}} {{1st}} *''[[The Empire Strikes Back: So You Want to Be a Jedi?]]'' {{Ab|The Empire Strikes Back: So You Want to Be a Jedi?
